key_insight: By deriving a principled occupancy field for oriented Gaussians, the paper converts 3D Gaussian Splatting from an opacity-driven renderer into a geometry-aware representation, enabling direct, high-fidelity surface extraction.
problem_solved: 3D Gaussian Splatting lacks a global geometric field, making accurate surface reconstruction difficult and forcing heuristic workarounds (e.g., TSDF fusion of blended depth maps).
method: Formulate an occupancy probability field for oriented Gaussians (inspired by Objects as Volumes) that aggregates per-Gaussian contributions into a global geometry field.
Provide an analytical / differentiable mapping from Gaussian parameters to occupancy so the model yields consistent volumetric values rather than only opacity splats.
Extract surfaces from the occupancy field using standard iso-surface techniques (e.g., marching cubes), producing high-fidelity meshes without heuristic depth fusion.
impact: Transforms fast, view-synthesis-focused Gaussian Splatting into a practical tool for accurate surface reconstruction, bridging the gap between real-time rendering and geometry-centric tasks (e.g., modeling, AR/VR, robotics).
visual_elements: Before vs after comparison: blobby Gaussian splats (opacity) vs crisp reconstructed mesh (occupancy-derived)
Pipeline diagram: oriented Gaussians -> occupancy field aggregation -> iso-surface extraction
Cross-section visualization showing per-Gaussian occupancy contributions and the resulting iso-surface
Quantitative bar chart: mesh accuracy / completeness vs TSDF fusion and implicit SDF baselines
paper_title: From Blobs to Spokes: High-Fidelity Surface Reconstruction via Oriented Gaussians
paper_authors: Diego Gomez, Antoine Guédon, Nissim Maruani, Bingchen Gong, Maks Ovsjanikov
